steps.text: Grease a 9x13 inch pan. In a large saucepan over medium heat, stir together the sugar and honey. Bring to a boil, then remove from heat and stir in the peanut butter until well blended. Stir in the cereal and if desired, stir in the salted peanuts. Press into the prepared pan. Allow to cool until firm, then cut into bars.

raw_recipe.headline: Oaty Cereal Bars
raw_recipe.description: Nutritious breakfast cereal smothered in a peanut butter and honey mixture to make a tasty portable breakfast.
raw_recipe.name: Oaty Cereal Bars

Bring to a boil, then remove from heat and stir in the peanut butter until well blended. Stir in the cereal and if desired, stir in the salted peanuts. Press into the prepared pan. Allow to cool until firm, then cut into bars.

review.reviewBody: I made this as described, however I boiled the sugar mixture for longer. I know from having worked with past recipes, candy and fudge making, is that to get up to the right temperature to solidify at room temperature you would need to boil for several minutes. In fact, I let the sugar/honey mixture boil (while mixing) for about 4-5 minutes. I had no difficulty with these forming bars at all after boiling for longer than it stated in the recipe. Although I found the recipe to have a rather strong honey taste my husband and children who are honey lovers really enjoyed it.

I doubled everything except the sugar, used only 1/3 cup, as stated in some of the reviews, & I added 3 cups Cheerios & 3 cups Rice Chex , added 1 cup unsalted peanuts & 1 cup of milk chocolate chips. It's a bit gooey if I leave out of the refrigerator, very tasty & not too sweet. My daughter & I loved them, my 3 year old granddaughter wanted to know "why I put chocolate chips?" She's a sweet lover like myself, so I told her I love chocolate. My 9 month old granddaughter wanted some but, couldn't have because of the honey. I will definitely make them again when 9 month old is a year old.

If making in a 9 x 13 pan, definitely double the recipe. I customized it this way: replaced 1/2 the sugar with xylitol sweetener (natural low calorie sweetener), agave instead of honey (use half of what is called for because agave is sweeter). I replaced 1/2 the cereal with Go Lean Crunch, then added dried fruit and a sprinkle of mini chocolate chips. Delicious! For easy spreading, spoon mixture into pan, cover with foil or wax paper and press with hands.

I followed other reviews and substituted/added other ingredients (almonds, raisins), increased boil time to 2 minutes, and doubled the recipe. I had to end up cutting into 24 squares to reach a size my kids could finish at one sitting. Next time, I will feel comfortable using healthier cereal because the recipe is sweet enough without added sugar. Great recipe, thank you! These are our new school day breakfast bar!

UPDATE: I made this recipe again and decided to try a 9x13 pan on a single recipe since the double recipe made a lot. I used Cheerios and all ingredients at the amount suggested and it did not make enough to fill the pan. I will now use an 8" for a single batch and 9x13 for a double.

I taste the PB more than the honey in this, and here's what I did (based on reading reviews): 1/2 cup sugar, 1/2 cup honey, 1/4 cup maple syrup - boiled that for about 45 seconds. Then added 1 cup PB along with about 1 tsp vanilla. Then added 2 cups cheerios, 2 cups rice krispies, and 1 cup grape nuts. Stirred in some butterscotch and mini chocolate chips - spread out in a 9x13 pyrex and then let cool. These were yummy, and very moist. I'm anxious to hear how the kids like them in their lunches tomorrow!

I'm on my second time making these in three days! Buttered 9x13 pan, 1 cup corn syrup, 2/3 c brown sugar, 1 cup crunchy pb, pinch of salt, 2 tsp vanilla, 10 cups of cereal (3 c Multigrain Cheerios, 3c Kix, and 4 c cocoa puffs). Once the syrup and sugar started bubbling around the edges, I timed one minute and then removed from the heat. Pressed into the pan using a sheet of waxed paper and allowed to cool before cutting. Once cool, cutting into bars is no problem. My next attempt will include oats, coconut, and chocolate chips...can't wait! Thank you for a wonderful base recipe!!

Very yummy! I used corn syrup instead of honey and chex instead of cheerios. I added a touch of vanilla too but would recommend adding a dash of salt if you aren't using salted peanuts because I think you'd want something to balance out the sweetness. I smooshed them down into the pan with a spoon sprayed with Pam to really compress them so they'd stay in bar form and they did perfectly. Will definitely make again but probably improvise more.

awesome recipe, easy to tweak, I used 2 cups of krispies, and 1 cup of fruity krispies in the first batch for the kiddos, The second batch lowcarb for my Mom and me, substituting 1/2 cup splenda for the sugar and "sugarfree" honey/sugar free "maple" syrup 50/50 and unsweetened wheat puffs, I suggest toasting the wheat puffs in the oven for 10 minutes first if you want them more crispy. These adjustment cut the carbs almost 75%!!! Oh happy day!!!
Easy recipe. Used vanilla sugar and added butterscotch chips when cooled a little. Will make again. Browned sugar before adding honey.

Was hesitant due to some of the sweetness reviews, but this is good! Double all ingredients except the sugar...use 1/3 c...use 9x13 pan. (I also stirred in a few mini-choc chips when the pb mix cooled a bit.) Kids loved 'em...hubby raved. Thanks for the recipe!

I made this twice already. The first time the only change I made is that I added 4 cups of mixed cereal and I boiled it for a few minutes. I was unable to cut it so I just broke it apart. The second time I didn't have enough honey so I substituted maple syrup for most of the honey. I used 4 cups of cereal again. I boiled the mixture a little less and this time (for about 1-1.5 minute) and I was able to cut it into bars. Both times my husband devoured them so it's definitely worth 5 starts even though I myself find them too sweet.

I made it twice and it was too hard when I took it out of the refrigerator. Even when I cut the time down. Is there anything I can add to make it softer? I have to microwave them to get them chewy . Thanks

Back in the 70’s and 80’s, my school cafeteria made these. They were a favorite for all the kids. This is the same recipe I got from them. But they are just a little different. Back then, they used less of the cereal so they were chewier. They must have run out cereal every week because I swear they only used a third of the cereal in this recipe.

Used some leftover bean cereal o’s that were not great to eat as a cereal. I made it with crunchy pb. I used half regular and half buckwheat honey. Reduced the sugar to 1/3 c and added half a cup of mini marshmallows. Super easy and very yummy.
One more note, I used a much smaller pan than 9x13. I would double the recipe for a 9x13.
Simple and great. I don't have a big sweet tooth, so I cut the sugar by a tad.

Great recipe. Very easy to make. I didn't have peanuts but I had the bottom of a tin of mixed nuts and fruit that I put in. I followed the suggestions and used less sugar. I also used the Kashi cereal that was being ignored.
Use 25% less ingredients for serving

"It's delicious...sometimes very hard to chew", said my daughter. That said, "hard to chew" may be a feature of even cereal bars that are mass-produced and sold in the grocery store. I think that's just how they are. Nonetheless, it was very tasty and satisfying. The cooking process is easy and rewarding. 

We used generic Cheerios. Not bad!

I cooked it for 5 minutes like it said, and they came out pretty hard, gonna cook it for a few minutes less. My fiance loves peanut butter, he said they were really good besides how hard they were. 
Thank you for the receipe!
